department: Graduate School for Cellular and Biomedical Sciences (GCB)

deadline.value: The GCB's next round closes on 15 December 2026, and rounds fall on 15 April, 15 August and 15 December; the page does not tie any round to an autumn 2027 start.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Candidates must arrange a research laboratory and a supervisor before applying to the GCB.
supervisor.quote: candidates must themselves arrange for a research laboratory and a supervisor

funding.value: The supervisor's acceptance letter includes a financial pledge, but no GCB page says that all or most students are funded.
funding.quote: Letter of acceptance by the supervisor, written on official letter paper, dated and signed, including a financial pledge.

entry_route.value: GCB applicants hold a master's degree or equivalent in life sciences, engineering, physics or computer science.
entry_route.quote: GCB applicants possess a master's degree or equivalent in life sciences or related areas

notes: Neuroscience and biomedical engineering are listed as also_fields because the GCB's own programme description covers them: "The GCB offers structured training in experimental research in the fields of biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, immunology, biomedical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, and biomedical engineering, leading to a PhD" (GCB Annual Report 2025, https://www.gcb.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/center_gradschools/gs_cb/content/e126792/e289326/e398724/files1798826/GCBAnnualReport2025_eng.pdf). The GCB rounds are 15 April, 15 August and 15 December. The GCB application page is cited for the supervisor rule; the 2025 annual report for the master's rule.
name: PhD programmes of the Graduate School for Cellular and Biomedical Sciences
